theory.intro: Earth rotates $360^{\circ}$ in $24\text{ hours}$, so in the idealised local solar-time model every $15^{\circ}$ of longitude equals a $1\text{ hour}$ time difference. Use this model for the longitude calculations below; civil time-zone boundaries do not strictly follow longitude.
facts: Earth rotates from west to east at $15^{\circ}\text{ longitude} = 1\text{ hour}$ ($1^{\circ} = 4\text{ minutes}$).
$\text{Time difference (hours)} = \dfrac{\text{Longitude difference}}{15^{\circ}}$ in the idealised local solar-time model.
Subtract longitudes for locations in the same hemisphere (both E or both W), and add them for opposite hemispheres.
The location further **east** is **ahead** in time, while the location further **west** is **behind**, using longitudes measured from Greenwich.
In the idealised local solar-time model, **latitude has no effect** on the calculated time difference; only longitude determines it.

For dated solar times, use signed longitudes relative to Greenwich: east is positive and west is negative. Each location's dated solar time is Greenwich time plus its signed longitude divided by $15$. If the longitude difference exceeds $180^{\circ}$, keep that difference rather than using the shortest angular separation.

When a local time is requested, add the difference for a location ahead or subtract it for a location behind. At or beyond $24{:}00$, subtract $24\text{ hours}$ and advance the day; for a negative result, add $24\text{ hours}$ and go back a day. Repeat if needed.
steps: Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)
Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours
Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)
If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day

workedExamples.question_text: Calculate the time difference between $A(22^{\circ}\text{S},125^{\circ}\text{W})$ and $B(48^{\circ}\text{N},35^{\circ}\text{W})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Both longitudes are west, so subtract. Latitude does not affect the time difference.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=125^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=90\div15\\&=6\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Calculate the time difference between $P(18^{\circ}\text{N},0^{\circ})$ and $Q(32^{\circ}\text{S},45^{\circ}\text{W})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
Calculate the time difference between $A(12^{\circ}\text{S},40^{\circ}\text{W})$ and $B(36^{\circ}\text{N},65^{\circ}\text{E})$ using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The longitudes are on opposite sides of Greenwich, so add.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=40^{\circ}+65^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=105\div15\\&=7\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Two stations are at $(8^{\circ}\text{S},117.5^{\circ}\text{E})$ and $(24^{\circ}\text{N},65^{\circ}\text{E})$. Calculate their time difference in hours and minutes using $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=117.5^{\circ}-65^{\circ}\\&=52.5^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=52.5\div15\\&=3.5\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

Convert the fractional hour to minutes.

$\begin{aligned}0.5\times60&=30\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

The time difference is $3\text{ h }30\text{ min}$.

workedExamples.question_text: At Town $A(16^{\circ}\text{S},95^{\circ}\text{W})$, the local solar time is $10{:}20\text{ am}$. Find the local solar time at Town $B(42^{\circ}\text{N},35^{\circ}\text{W})$. Use $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=95^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=60\div15\\&=4\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$35^{\circ}\text{W}$ is east of $95^{\circ}\text{W}$, so Town $B$ is ahead. Add the difference.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }B&=10{:}20+4\text{ hours}\\&=14{:}20\end{aligned}$

It is $2{:}20\text{ pm}$ at Town $B$ on the same day.

workedExamples.question_text:
Use longitude-based solar times and $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.

(a) A presentation starts at $6{:}40\text{ pm}$ Thursday at $A(54^{\circ}\text{N},25^{\circ}\text{E})$. When does it start at $B(28^{\circ}\text{S},145^{\circ}\text{E})$?

(b) A live broadcast starts at $7{:}15\text{ am}$ Tuesday at $C(30^{\circ}\text{N},125^{\circ}\text{E})$. When does it start at $D(46^{\circ}\text{N},10^{\circ}\text{W})$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=145^{\circ}-25^{\circ}\\&=120^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=120\div15\\&=8\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$B$ is east of $A$, so add $8\text{ hours}$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }B&=18{:}40+8\text{ hours}\\&=26{:}40\\&=02{:}40\text{ Friday}\end{aligned}$

The presentation starts at $2{:}40\text{ am}$ Friday at $B$.

(b)

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=125^{\circ}+10^{\circ}\\&=135^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=135\div15\\&=9\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$D$ is west of $C$, so subtract $9\text{ hours}$. Add $24\text{ hours}$ to the negative result and go back a day.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time at }D&=7\text{ h }15\text{ min}-9\text{ h}\\&=-1\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=-1\text{ h }45\text{ min}+24\text{ h}\\&=22\text{ h }15\text{ min}\end{aligned}$

The broadcast starts at $10{:}15\text{ pm}$ Monday at $D$.

workedExamples.question_text: A plane leaves $A(0^{\circ},47^{\circ}\text{E})$ at $8{:}30\text{ pm}$ Wednesday for $B(0^{\circ},107^{\circ}\text{E})$. The flight takes $7\text{ h }45\text{ min}$. Find the local day and time at $B$ when it arrives. Use longitude-based solar times and $15^{\circ}=1\text{ hour}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=107^{\circ}-47^{\circ}\\&=60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=60\div15\\&=4\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

$B$ is east of $A$, so it is $4\text{ hours}$ ahead. First find the departure time at $B$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure time at }B&=20{:}30+4\text{ hours}\\&=24{:}30\\&=00{:}30\text{ Thursday}\end{aligned}$

Then add the flight duration.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival time at }B&=00{:}30+7\text{ h }45\text{ min}\\&=08{:}15\text{ Thursday}\end{aligned}$

The plane arrives at $8{:}15\text{ am}$ Thursday, local solar time.

workedExamples.question_text: A ship leaves Port $A(12^{\circ}\text{N},130^{\circ}\text{W})$ at $9{:}45\text{ am}$ Monday for Port $B(20^{\circ}\text{S},170^{\circ}\text{E})$. The voyage takes $14\text{ hours}$. Find the time difference and the local day and time at $B$ on arrival. All times are longitude-based solar times. For dates, use Greenwich time plus signed longitude divided by $15$, with east positive and west negative; do not use the shortest angular separation.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use signed longitudes relative to Greenwich.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Longitude difference}&=170^{\circ}-(-130^{\circ})\\&=300^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time difference}&=300\div15\\&=20\text{ hours}\end{aligned}$

Under the stated date convention, Port $B$ is $20\text{ hours}$ ahead. First find the departure time at $B$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Departure time at }B&=09{:}45+20\text{ hours}\\&=29{:}45\\&=05{:}45\text{ Tuesday}\end{aligned}$

Then add the voyage duration.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Arrival time at }B&=05{:}45+14\text{ hours}\\&=19{:}45\text{ Tuesday}\end{aligned}$

The ship arrives at $7{:}45\text{ pm}$ Tuesday, local solar time.

foundation.question_text: Calculate the time difference between $(28^{\circ}\text{S}, 135^{\circ}\text{W})$ and $(64^{\circ}\text{N}, 60^{\circ}\text{W})$.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
Both locations are in the Western hemisphere ($135^{\circ}\text{W}$ and $60^{\circ}\text{W}$).
$\text{Longitude difference} = 135^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{75^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}}$
$= 5\text{ hours}$

development.question_text:
City $A(40^{\circ}\text{N}, 15^{\circ}\text{E})$ has a local solar time of $3{:}00\text{ pm}$.
What is the local solar time at City $B(10^{\circ}\text{S}, 75^{\circ}\text{E})$ on the same day?
development.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 75^{\circ} - 15^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{60^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 4\text{ hours}$
3. **Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)**
City $B$ ($75^{\circ}\text{E}$) is further East than City $A$ ($15^{\circ}\text{E}$), so City $B$ is ahead.
4. **If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day**
$\text{Time at } B = 15{:}00 + 4\text{ hours}$
$= 19{:}00$
$= 7{:}00\text{ pm}$

development.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 150^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 120^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{120^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 8\text{ hours}$
3. **Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)**
Town $Y$ ($30^{\circ}\text{E}$) is further West than Town $X$ ($150^{\circ}\text{E}$), so Town $Y$ is behind.
4. **If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day**
$\text{Time at } Y = 11{:}00 - 8\text{ hours}$
$= 03{:}00$
$= 3{:}00\text{ am}$

mastery.question_text:
Linköping in Sweden is located at $(58^{\circ}\text{N}, 16^{\circ}\text{E})$ and Sydney in Australia is located at $(33^{\circ}\text{S}, 151^{\circ}\text{E})$.
Isabella in Sydney must attend an online presentation hosted in Linköping at $5{:}00\text{ pm}$ Thursday, local Swedish solar time.
What time and day in Sydney should Isabella log in? (Apply $15^{\circ} = 1\text{ hour}$; ignore daylight saving).
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 151^{\circ} - 16^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{135^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 9\text{ hours}$
3. **Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)**
Sydney ($151^{\circ}\text{E}$) is further East than Linköping ($16^{\circ}\text{E}$), so Sydney is $9\text{ hours}$ ahead.
4. **If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day**
$\text{Sydney time} = 17{:}00 + 9\text{ hours} = 26{:}00$
$26{:}00 - 24{:}00 = 02{:}00\text{ (next day)}$
Isabella should log in at $2{:}00\text{ am}$ on Friday.

mastery.question_text:
An aircraft departs a town in Kenya $(0^{\circ}, 38^{\circ}\text{E})$ on Tuesday at $10{:}00\text{ pm}$ and flies east to a town in Borneo $(0^{\circ}, 113^{\circ}\text{E})$.
The flight duration is $9\text{ hours}$.
Calculate the time difference from longitudes and state the local day and time in Borneo when the aircraft arrives. Use the longitude-based solar-time model for both the given departure time and the requested arrival time.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
$\text{Longitude difference} = 113^{\circ} - 38^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{75^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 5\text{ hours}$
3. **Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)**
Borneo ($113^{\circ}\text{E}$) is further East than Kenya ($38^{\circ}\text{E}$), so Borneo is $5\text{ hours}$ ahead.
4. **If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day**
$\text{Departure time in Borneo} = 22{:}00\text{ Tuesday} + 5\text{ hours} = 03{:}00\text{ Wednesday}$
$\text{Arrival time} = 03{:}00 + 9\text{ hours} = 12{:}00\text{ pm}$
The aircraft arrives in Borneo at $12{:}00\text{ pm}$ (noon) on Wednesday, local solar time.

mastery.question_text:
A ship departs Port $A(15^{\circ}\text{N}, 140^{\circ}\text{W})$ at $8{:}30\text{ am}$ on Monday on a $12\text{-hour}$ voyage towards Port $B(25^{\circ}\text{S}, 175^{\circ}\text{E})$.
Calculate the time difference between the ports using their longitudes, and find the local day and time at Port $B$ when the ship arrives. All given and requested times are longitude-based solar times. For dates, use Greenwich time plus the signed longitude divided by $15$, with east positive and west negative; do not use the shortest angular separation.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the difference in longitude (subtract for same hemisphere, add for opposite hemispheres)**
Use signed longitudes relative to Greenwich:
$\text{Longitude difference} = 175^{\circ} - (-140^{\circ}) = 315^{\circ}$
2. **Divide the longitude difference by $15^{\circ}$ to find the time difference in hours**
$\text{Time difference} = \dfrac{315^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 21\text{ hours}$
3. **Determine which location is further East (ahead) or West (behind)**
Port $B$ ($175^{\circ}\text{E}$) is $21\text{ hours}$ ahead of Port $A$ ($140^{\circ}\text{W}$) under the stated Greenwich/date convention.
4. **If a local time is requested, add or subtract the time difference and adjust the day**
$\text{Departure time at Port } B = 08{:}30\text{ Monday} + 21\text{ hours} = 29{:}30 = 05{:}30\text{ Tuesday}$
$\text{Arrival time at Port } B = 05{:}30\text{ Tuesday} + 12\text{ hours} = 17{:}30\text{ Tuesday}$
The ship arrives at $5{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday, local solar time.
